title: Soft-Shift Orchestration Notebook
content:
Context / intent:
This is a personal scratchbook for a 'soft shift' deployment pattern I want to try for low-risk model flips on Dedicated and Private fleets. Goal: enable a near-instant model variant switch for small cohorts without the heavy weight of traditional canaries (no full A/B infra) while keeping fast rollback and clear telemetry gates.

Top-level idea (one-liner):
- Stage new model on a small set of workers, shift a thin routing fraction that prefers low-risk sessions (idle, short seqs, dev clients) and then expand by doubling fractions with checks. If anything smells, flip wiring back and mark cohort tainted.

Quick checklist (operational):
- [ ] Build image with model_vX (tagged: model_vX-softshift-<date>)
- [ ] Push to image registry and verify digest in registry UI
- [ ] Update route config: create routing rule "softshift_vX_anchor" with initial weight 0.1%
- [ ] Identify warmup cohort (5 tenants/dev keys) and schedule quiet window
- [ ] Prepare rollback artifact: model_vW-stable pinned to fallback routing rule
- [ ] Post a Slack alert to #ops-rollouts announcing start and pinned toggles

Cohort selection heuristics (practical):
- Prefer: dev accounts, internal QA keys, short-turnaround sessions (<64 tokens), low token budgets
- Exclude: latency-sensitive premium tenants, scheduled batch jobs, long-context sessions (>1024 tokens)
- Use client metadata where possible: SDK versions flagged for canary opt-in, internal agent headers, test tenants list (from /shared/qa/softshift-keys)

Ramp plan (timing + fractions):
- Step 0: 0.1% to warmup cohort for 30 minutes – verify correctness, no OOMs, trace samples look good
- Step 1: 1% for 1 hour – traffic evenly distributed across multiple racks/regions if possible
- Step 2: 5% for 2 hours – enable thin caching (prefix cache disabled for new variant initially)
- Step 3: 15% for 3 hours – enable cache, observe cost/perf delta
- Step 4: 50% for 6 hours – full observability checks, user sentiment monitor on
- Step 5: 100% – after business signoff or automated pass

Telemetry and gating signals (must-check):
- Latency p50/p95 increase > 15% => HOLD and investigate
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) relative increase > 0.5% absolute => ROLL BACK
- OOM or host eviction events => IMMEDIATE ROLLBACK
- Inference QPS drop > 20% for 5 consecutive minutes => HOLD
- Quality signal (eval set shard) avg similarity drop > 3% => HOLD and manual review

Lightweight instrumentation to attach:
- Add route-tag metadata on traces so we can filter new variant traces quickly
- Auto-snapshot 100 model outputs from new variant every 15m and push to /tmp/softshift-samples/<timestamp> (for quick diff)
- Alert on both absolute token spend and per-token CPU GPU utilization per instance group

Warmup and priming notes (how to avoid cold-snap):
- Don’t enable prefix cache for the first two ramp steps. We want to catch correctness issues without cached state masking them.
- Run scripted priming payloads (small sequence + expected response shape) hitting each new worker after rollout step begins
- For transformers with heavy KV, send a 64-token warmup sequence across 3 different batch sizes to initialize caches

Version pinning considerations (per-tenant):
- Keep a per-tenant pin map for the first 48 hours (clients still on previous version if flagged): this reduces blast radius if some tenants have stateful expectations
- Add lightweight API for customer-success to request a pin/unpin: track requests as CS-<date>-softshift tickets

Rollback playbook (fast path):
- Criteria: any IMMEDIATE ROLLBACK signal or >2 gating signals within 30 minutes
- Steps:
  1) Flip route to pinned fallback (model_vW-stable) via console toggle (or API)
  2) Announce rollback in Slack with timestamp and reason
  3) Snapshot diagnostics (logs, core dumps, GPU metrics) and attach to JIRA
  4) Start post-mortem doc draft (use template PMT-rollback-softshift)

Observability cheat-sheet (where to look):
- Console -> per-route latency heatmaps (filter: new route tag)
- Traces -> sample new-variant traces; compare op durations (decoder, kv fetch, kernel time)
- Infra -> GPU mem pressure / p99 allocator stalls / context switches
- Billing -> per-token runtime cost delta (if >10% increase, raise cost review)

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- How to programmatically pick which racks to avoid for warmup? (prefer lower-utilized ones)
- Should we pre-provision burst capacity for step-3 to avoid throttling in Dedicated? TBD with infra
- Need a tiny dashboard widget that shows last 100 sample diffs (human readable) in Console
- Confirm product/legal signoff for customer-facing changes to model outputs (especially private deployments)

Quick failure scenarios I want to simulate before real runs:
- Sim A: memory leak after 45 minutes under 5% traffic – run for 2 hours and validate stability
- Sim B: degraded token quality but identical latency – trigger eval pipeline with seeded prompts
- Sim C: partial rack eviction (one AZ) – ensure routing fallback respects region policies

Post-roll notes & artifacts to produce (on success or rollback):
- Tag container images with rollout metadata and annotate GitHub PR
- Write short debrief: what we saw at each step (metrics + notable traces)
- Update runbook with any missing observability hooks found during the run

Random scribbles / heuristics to remember:
- Prefer slower, predictable ramp over quick jumps during US morning hours
- Night runs: avoid customers in EU business hours unless they’re on the warmup list
- If something odd but non-critical shows up, hold and escalate to ML lead for 30 mins before rollback (documented decision)

Slack snippet to copy when starting:
"Heads-up: kicking off soft-shift for model_vX at 2026-03-12T22:00Z. Initial 0.1% warmup cohort (dev keys only). Will post updates at each ramp step or on trigger. Ping @oncall if any immediate rollback needed."

End of notebook. Keep iterating.
